title: Transfer RSUs from Morgan Stanley to India (Shares and Cash)
summary: How Indian employees can move vested RSUs out of Morgan Stanley at Work (StockPlan Connect, Shareworks): transfer the shares or sell and wire the proceeds.
body_markdown:
If your employer's RSUs are held with Morgan Stanley, you have two ways to get them out of the stock plan account once they vest. You can transfer the shares to another account in your name without selling, or you can sell and send the US dollar proceeds wherever you want to invest next.


Which one suits you depends on what you plan to do with the shares. If you want to keep holding the stock, a transfer avoids a taxable sale. If you were going to sell anyway, moving cash is simpler.


This guide covers both routes and the Indian tax treatment of each. For the general rules that apply at every broker, see[Can I transfer my RSUs to another broker?](https://paasa.com/blog/can-i-transfer-my-rsus-to-another-broker)


## Table of contents


- Which Morgan Stanley platform are you on?
- What you can do in StockPlan Connect
- Moving shares from Morgan Stanley
- Moving cash from Morgan Stanley
- Tax and reporting after the move
- About Paasa


## Which Morgan Stanley platform are you on?


Morgan Stanley has run employee equity plans on more than one platform, which is why colleagues at different companies describe different screens. Its own[stock plan FAQ](https://www.morganstanley.com/atwork/employees/stockplan-faq-sw) now uses one name, the Morgan Stanley at Work stock plan account, for what was previously called Shareworks, StockPlan Connect or the E*TRADE stock plan account.


Your login page and the menus you see still depend on which of these your employer uses. The rules that matter for a transfer are the same on all of them:


- Only vested shares that your company has released can be sold or moved.
- Your company's trading windows and holding rules continue to apply while the shares are in the plan.
- The options you are shown can differ by country, so what a US colleague sees may not match your screen.


Your holdings and your vesting schedule are both shown in the stock plan account, so check there to see which shares have vested before you plan a move.


## What you can do in StockPlan Connect


Morgan Stanley's public material on StockPlan Connect describes a small set of actions, and these are the ones that matter when you plan a move.


- **Check your awards and vesting.** Morgan Stanley's[StockPlan Connect overview](https://www.morganstanley.com/cs/pdf/604892698_CRC_2714723_StockPlan_Connect_Overview_020420.pdf) says you can check award vesting schedules and sell shares from the mobile app.
- **Complete your tax certification.** The same overview says that if a tax recertification is due, you have to complete it on the website or app before you can use any other feature.
- **Choose how sale proceeds reach you.** The overview lists a wire, a deposit into your StockPlan Connect account, and international ACH in a few currencies.
- **Save your bank details.** Morgan Stanley's wire setup guide for StockPlan Connect shows the path: click your profile name, open "Manage Banking Information", choose a delivery method, enter the bank details and confirm with the security code. Delivery methods vary by country.


Dividends follow the delivery method you have chosen. If it is set to cash, Morgan Stanley says the cash is deposited into your StockPlan Connect holdings account, where it stays until you choose to send it out.


## Moving shares from Morgan Stanley


A transfer of shares moves the same shares into another account in your name. Nothing is sold, so there is no capital gain in India.


Morgan Stanley's[support centre](https://www.morganstanley.com/atwork/employees/support/support-center/how-do-i-sell-or-transact-on-my-shares) describes this for the Shareworks platform. When you start a transaction on vested shares, you choose between selling them and a "Shares Withdrawal", which transfers the shares to a brokerage account by electronic transfer to the broker. You receive a confirmation and a reference number once the withdrawal is submitted.


How the shares travel depends on the account they sit in. Shares in a regular Morgan Stanley brokerage account move to Paasa through ACATS, the standard US system for moving assets between brokerage firms, typically in 3 to 5 business days, and[How ACATS works for Indian investors](https://paasa.com/blog/how-acats-works-for-indian-investors) explains it in detail. Shares still in the stock plan account move through Morgan Stanley's own share transfer process, such as the Shares Withdrawal above, which can take longer.


Because the screens differ by platform and by country, start with the receiving side. Tell the Paasa team that your shares are in a Morgan Stanley stock plan account and which platform you use, and they will guide you through the process before you submit anything on the Morgan Stanley side.


Two practical points apply before you begin:


- Download your statements and the vesting history for every tranche. You will need the vesting dates and values for your Indian return.
- Make sure your name on the stock plan account matches your name on the receiving account.


## Moving cash from Morgan Stanley


The other route is to sell in the stock plan account and send the proceeds out. Morgan Stanley's support centre says shares can be sold immediately at the market price or with a limit price that can stay open for up to 30 days.


At the end of the sale you reach a "Delivery Instructions" step, where you choose how the money is sent. According to Morgan Stanley's page on[receiving net proceeds](https://www.morganstanley.com/atwork/support/how-can-i-receive-the-net-proceeds-from-my-transaction) , the choices depend on your country and your company's rules, and a wire to a bank account is one of them.


Morgan Stanley says net proceeds are typically credited shortly after the settlement date of the sale. It also warns that service fees may apply to some delivery methods, that your own bank may charge for receiving a wire, and that a payment rejected by the bank can be delayed by 5 to 10 business days. Entering the bank details carefully is worth the extra minute.


To send the proceeds to Paasa, the steps in the app are:


- **Step 1:** Download the Paasa app and complete your KYC to open your account, if you have not already.
- **Step 2:** Open the app and tap "Transfer investments".
- **Step 3:** Select Morgan Stanley as your broker.
- **Step 4:** Select "Transfer cash".
- **Step 5:** Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the transfer.


Always confirm the account details Paasa provides before you submit the wire. If you want someone to walk you through your Morgan Stanley dashboard first, write to support@paasa.com or message your relationship manager in the app.


Money that goes from Morgan Stanley to another account abroad never enters India, so it is not a remittance under LRS. What does apply is the[FEMA 180-day rule](https://paasa.com/blog/fema-180-day-rule) , under which sale proceeds held abroad have to be reinvested or brought back to India within 180 days.


## Tax and reporting after the move


The two routes are taxed differently, and this is usually what decides between them.


Transfer the shares Sell and move cash


Is it a sale in India? No Yes


Capital gains tax None because of the move On the gain since vesting


Cost of acquisition Unchanged Used to compute the gain


Holding period Keeps running from the vesting date Ends on the sale date


Schedule FA Still applies Applies to the year of sale and to what you buy next


A transfer of shares between two accounts that both belong to you is not a sale. Your cost stays the rupee value that was taxed as salary when the shares vested, and the holding period continues from the vesting date.


If you sell, the gain is the sale value minus that cost. Shares held for 24 months or less give a short-term gain taxed at your slab rate, and shares held for more than 24 months give a long-term gain taxed at 12.5%.[Capital gains tax on RSU shares](https://paasa.com/blog/capital-gains-tax-rsu-shares) covers the calculation, and[How foreign RSUs are taxed in India](https://paasa.com/blog/how-rsus-are-taxed-in-india) covers the tax at vesting.


Schedule FA still applies after the move. If you are resident and ordinarily resident, you report the shares and the foreign account that holds them for every calendar year in which you held them. In the year of the move, the Morgan Stanley account and the new account were both held during the calendar year, so both are reported. See[Schedule FA for RSU holders](https://paasa.com/blog/schedule-fa-rsu-holders) .


## About Paasa


[Paasa](https://paasa.com/rsu) is a global investing platform built for Indian and Asian investors, giving you direct access to stocks and ETFs across the US, UK, Europe and Asia from one account.


- **Move shares without selling:** Transfer directly from Fidelity, Morgan Stanley or Schwab through an ACATS transfer, typically in 3 to 5 business days, with guidance for your specific broker.
- **Diversify once the shares arrive:** Invest in markets across 11 countries, including European-domiciled UCITS ETFs that are estate-tax safe for Indian residents.
- **Tax reports built for your ITR:** Year-end reports aligned with Indian ITR requirements, including Schedule CG and Schedule FA, are sent automatically and can be shared with your CA.
